title: AI Module 1: Inheritance
lessonSummary: Great! Your child class inherits everything from its parent.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a child class inherits a method.
Write the class Robot with `__init__(self, name)` and `introduce(self)` (prints I am Nova.) and the child class BattleRobot(Robot) with only `pass`. Create BattleRobot("Nova") and call `introduce()`.

tasks.instruction: The class Robot is given. Write RepairRobot(Robot) with a **new** method `arm(self)` that prints Orbit charges the laser. (name from `self`). Create RepairRobot("Orbit") and call `introduce()` first, then `arm()`.

validation.expected:
I am Orbit.
Orbit charges the laser.

tasks.instruction: The classes Robot, BattleRobot(Robot) and RepairRobot(Robot) are given. Create BattleRobot("Nova") and check with `isinstance` whether it belongs to Robot and whether it belongs to RepairRobot. Print both results on two lines.

lessonSummary: Nice! Children may do things differently from their parents.

title: AI Module 3: super() and __init__
lessonSummary: Well done! You connect parent and child with super().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: a constructor with super().

The class Robot is given. Write BattleRobot(Robot) with `__init__(self, name, armor=30)` that sets the name via `super().__init__(name)` and stores `armor`. Create BattleRobot("Nova", 45) and print exactly Nova 45.
The class Robot is given. Write RepairRobot(Robot) with `__init__(self, name, tools=50)` and `super()`. Create RepairRobot("Orbit") without a second value and print exactly Orbit 50.

The classes Robot and BattleRobot (with an overridden `work`) are given. Write Elite(BattleRobot) that overrides `work`: first `super().work()`, then a second line Nova is a master!. Create Elite("Nova") and call `work()`.

validation.expected:
Nova fires the laser.
Nova is a master!

tasks.instruction: Run this example: the same method, three classes.

validation.expected:
Zeta idles.
Nova fires the laser.
Orbit repairs the hull.

tasks.instruction: The classes Robot, BattleRobot and RepairRobot are given. Write a function `los(figure)` that calls `figure.work()`. Call it for BattleRobot("Nova") and RepairRobot("Orbit") one after the other.

validation.expected:
Nova fires the laser.
Orbit repairs the hull.

The classes are given. Write your **own** class Spectator **without parents** with `work(self)` that prints The crew cheers.. Call `work()` for a list with BattleRobot("Nova") and Spectator() one after the other (duck typing).

The crew cheers.

title: Extra Challenge 4: Everything Together
lessonSummary: Done: inheritance, dictionaries, randomness and JSON work together!

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – dictionary of classes: the classes are given. Build `klassen = {"BattleRobot": BattleRobot, "RepairRobot": RepairRobot}` and create an object through the name `klassen["BattleRobot"]("Nova")`. Call `work()`.
Step 2 – randomness: the classes are given. Pick a class with `random.choice([BattleRobot, RepairRobot])`, create an object from it and print `isinstance(object, Robot)` (True).

Step 3 – save as JSON: the classes are given. Create BattleRobot("Nova") and build `daten = {"typ": type(f).__name__, "name": f.name}` (`type(f).__name__` gives the class name as text). Print `json.dumps(daten)`.

Step 4 – load JSON: the classes and the text `text = '{"typ": "BattleRobot", "name": "Nova"}'` are given. Read it with `json.loads`, look up the class in the dictionary `klassen` and rebuild the object. Call `work()`.
